# Machine Learning Approaches for Detecting Fake News Generated by AI

## Overview

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and the widespread use of digital media platforms have significantly increased the generation and dissemination of fake news. AI-generated content poses a serious threat to information credibility, making automated fake news detection systems increasingly important.

This project explores and compares multiple machine learning approaches for detecting fake news articles using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. Both traditional machine learning models and transformer-based deep learning models are evaluated and compared.

The project is developed as part of academic research at:

**Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences**  
Frankfurt am Main, Germany

## Abstract

This study focuses on exploring and comparing multiple machine learning approaches for detecting fake news generated by artificial intelligence.

A comparative analysis of five different models is conducted:

- Logistic Regression
- Naive Bayes
- Support Vector Machine (SVM)
- Random Forest
- BERT (Transformer-based model)

A publicly available dataset consisting of labeled real and fake news articles is utilized for training and evaluation.

The dataset undergoes preprocessing steps such as:

- Text normalization
- Lowercasing
- Punctuation removal
- Duplicate removal
- Feature preparation

For traditional machine learning models, TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency) is used for feature extraction, while contextual embeddings are planned for the BERT model.

The performance of each model is evaluated using:

- Accuracy
- Precision
- Recall
- F1-score

The objective is to identify the most effective approach and analyze the trade-offs between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy.

# Dataset

The dataset contains labeled news articles classified as:

- Real News
- Fake News

The dataset includes:

- News title
- Article text
- Labels

The preprocessing pipeline combines the title and article text into a unified text representation for improved NLP performance.

---

# Methodology

## 1. Data Preprocessing

The preprocessing pipeline performs:

- Missing value removal
- Duplicate removal
- Text normalization
- Lowercasing
- Punctuation removal
- Column cleaning

The final dataset used for training contains:

- `text`
- `label`

---

## 2. Train/Test Split

The dataset is divided into:

- 80% training data
- 20% testing data

Stratified splitting is used to preserve label distribution.

---

## 3. Feature Extraction

### TF-IDF Vectorization

Traditional machine learning models use TF-IDF vectorization to convert text into numerical feature vectors.

The vectorizer includes:

- English stopword removal
- Unigrams and bigrams
- Minimum document frequency filtering

---

## 4. Machine Learning Models

The following models are implemented and compared:

### Logistic Regression
A strong baseline linear classifier commonly used for text classification tasks.

### Naive Bayes
A probabilistic model effective for sparse text representations.

### Support Vector Machine (SVM)
A high-performing linear classifier particularly effective for TF-IDF text data.

### Random Forest
An ensemble learning model using multiple decision trees.

### BERT
A transformer-based deep learning model capable of learning contextual semantic representations.

---

# Evaluation Metrics

The following evaluation metrics are used:

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Overall prediction correctness |
| Precision | Correct positive predictions |
| Recall | Ability to detect positive samples |
| F1-score | Harmonic mean of precision and recall |

# Installation

## Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Hanan-Nawaz/fake_news_ai
cd fake-news-ai
```

---

## Install dependencies

Using uv:

```bash
uv sync
```

Or manually:

```bash
uv add pandas scikit-learn numpy transformers torch
```

---

# Usage

## Run Classical ML Pipeline

```bash
uv run python -m scripts.train_classical
```

---

## Run BERT Pipeline

```bash
uv run python -m scripts.train_bert
```
